title: Designing a Bioreactor to Improve Data Acquisition and Model the Throughput of Engineered Cardiac Tissues
protocol: Perform all cell and hECT manipulation in aseptic conditions in a HEPA-filtered class II biological safety cabinet or laminar flow work bench.
Sterilize all non-sterile solutions by filtration through a 0.22 μm filter.
Maintain all cells and hECTs in an incubator at 37 °C, 95% relative humidity, and 5% CO2.
Machine the baseplate out of PTFE according to schematics using a CNC mill.
Fabricate aluminum master cast for bioreactor components.
Machine the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) rack negative master cast out of aluminum according to the schematics in Figure 1B.
Drill six evenly spaced holes of 0.5 mm diameter for creating PDMS posts.
Machine the bioreactor frame out of polysulfone according to the schematics in Figure 1C.
Machine the aluminum cast holder out of aluminum according to the schematics in Figure 1D.
Print two PDMS rack casting apparatus brackets using a thermoplastic fused deposition modeling 3D printer.
Place four aluminum negative master casts in the cast holder such that post holes align with the dead space opposite the triangle shelves.
Wrap the apparatus in a rectangular piece of 0.5 mm thick silicone sheeting as a gasket to prevent leakage.
Clamp the wrapped apparatus between two parallel 3D printed brackets using a screw clamp.
Mix 0.5 mL of PDMS curing agent with 5 mL of PDMS elastomer base at a 1:10 ratio in a shallow container vigorously for 5 min.
Degass the PDMS mixture in a vacuum chamber until bubbles disappear by applying a strong vacuum (0.1-1 kPa) for 20-60 min.
Pour the degassed PDMS mixture onto the casting apparatus, overfilling to ensure complete coverage of each slot.
If desired, add small, colored glass beads opposite the side with posts in the body of the PDMS racks for unique identification.
Return the casting apparatus to the vacuum chamber and apply a strong vacuum horizontally level for at least 12 h.
Allow the PDMS to cure at room temperature away from dust for about 48 h.
Remove the clamp, brackets, and silicone sheeting from the casting apparatus.
Trim away the PDMS film on top of the casting apparatus and frame supports using a stainless-steel razor blade.
Gently separate the PDMS racks from the sides of the cast holder using fingers.
Insert a blunted stainless-steel razorblade into the dead space between the cast and the cast holder, prying them apart to ensure that the PDMS filling the dead space remains with the cast holder.
Cut away the remaining PDMS films using a sharp stainless-steel blade.
Cut the dead-space PDMS from the tips of the posts.
Free the PDMS rack from the cast, starting with the side opposite the posts and working on alternate sides until the posts are free of the master casts.
Repeat the previous step until all PDMS racks and posts are freed.
Trim away any remaining excess PDMS from the racks using a sharp razor blade.

Print the components of the SPoT casting apparatus using a thermoplastic fused deposition modeling 3D printer with a layer height of 0.1 mm, wall/bottom/top thickness of 1 mm, infill density of 80%, printing temperature of 230 °C, build plate temperature of 70 °C, and a brim for adhesion.
Ensure a secure press fit between the 3D-printed pieces and confirm that PDMS racks fit snugly with posts reaching bottoms of wells without bending.
Trim/file plastic if necessary to ensure proper fit.
Mix 0.5 mL of black PDMS part A with 0.5 mL of part B thoroughly until uniform in color.
Degas mixed black PDMS in a vacuum chamber under strong vacuum for 20 min.
Pour degassed black PDMS onto the 3D-printed base to fill holes and tap to ensure no bubbles remain.
Scrape away excess PDMS off the base as much as possible.
Snap three-pronged piece onto the base.
Place PDMS racks in grooves on the three-pronged jig with ends of posts dipping into black PDMS in circular wells.
Cure black PDMS at room temperature and protected from dust for 48 h.
Slide out the three-pronged piece, minimizing tension on the posts.
Use small forceps to scrape away the thin film of black PDMS that surrounds each SPoT.
Insert fine-tipped bent forceps into the SPoT well to free it from the 3D-printed base.
Inspect the SPoTs.
Trim away any remaining black PDMS film using fine Vannas scissors.
Ensure that the finished posts are of the correct length by fitting the PDMS racks onto the polysulfone frame and then sliding this onto the black baseplate.
Pair the PDMS racks, and add them to the frame using the frame tabs.
Autoclave in a bag with a PTFE baseplate for at least a 30 min cycle.
Coat a cell-culture-treated 6-well plate with qualified basement membrane matrix diluted in 1:1 DMEM/F12.
Incubate the coated plate at 37 °C for at least 30 min.
Prepare 500 mL of iPSC culture medium according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Add 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin (10,000 IU/mL to 10,000 µg/mL) stock solution to the culture medium.
Aspirate the medium from the wells containing iPSCs.
Wash each well once with 1 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Add 1 mL of iPSC dissociation solution per well.
Incubate in a laminar flow hood for 1 min.
Aspirate the iPSC dissociation solution.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C without medium for 5 min.
Add 1 mL of 2 µM thiazovivin in iPSC medium to neutralize the iPSC dissociation solution.
Use a 2 mL serological pipette to dissociate colonies into clumps of roughly 10 cells.
Wash each well with an additional 1 mL of 2 µM thiazovivin in iPSC medium.
Add 2 mL of cell suspension to each well of the plate newly coated with basement membrane matrix.
After 24 h, remove the medium from the wells.
Add fresh iPSC medium (without thiazovivin) to the wells.
Feed the iPSCs every 48 h with 2 mL of iPSC medium.
Feed the iPSCs every 72 h with 4 mL of medium.
Replate the cells at a 1:6 dilution for passaging every 3 days or when they reach 80% confluence.
Begin the differentiation when iPSC monolayers are 80%-90% confluent.

Prepare the differentiation medium by adding 10 mL of B27 supplement without insulin and 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin stock solution to 500 mL of Roswell Park Memorial Institute 1640 medium (RPMI).
Prepare the cardiomyocyte maintenance medium by adding 10 mL of B27 supplement and 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin stock solution to 500 mL of RPMI 1640.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 on Day 0.
Add 2 mL of 10 µM CHIR99021 and diluted basement membrane matrix in differentiation medium on Day 0.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 after 24 hours or when cell confluence is below 70% on Day 1.
Add 2 mL of differentiation medium to the cells on Day 1.
Incubate for 48 h after adding differentiation medium on Day 1.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 on Days 3 and 4.
Add 2 mL of 5 µM IWR-1 in differentiation medium to the cells on Days 3 and 4.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 on Days 5 and 6.
Add 2 mL of differentiation medium to the cells on Days 5 and 6.
Wash the cells with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 on Days 7, 8, 9, and 10.
Add 2 mL of cardiomyocyte maintenance medium to the cells on Days 7, 8, 9, and 10.
Replace the medium with 4 mL of fresh cardiomyocyte maintenance medium every 48-72 hours starting from Day 11 onwards.
Aspirate and pipette slowly to avoid damaging vigorously beating monolayers during media replacement.
Harvest cardiomyocyte monolayers 8-60 days post-differentiation induction.
Rinse each well of cardiomyocytes twice with 2 mL of PBS.
Add 1 mL of room-temperature 0.25% trypsin-EDTA to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C for 5-10 min until cells appear rounded and will detach with light tapping of the plate.
Add 1 mL of 10% FBS in cardiomyocyte maintenance medium to each well to neutralize the dissociation.
Gently pipette the monolayers using a 5 mL serological pipette tip.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 50 mL conical tube to break up the pellet into clumps of 10-20 cells.
Mix the cell suspension by inverting the conical tube.
Transfer 10 µL of cells to 10 µL of trypan blue for counting.
Count the cells using an automated cell counter or glass hemocytometer.
Separate the cell suspension appropriately if not all the cells will be used or set aside some cells for flow cytometry.
Centrifuge the cells at 250 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate as much supernatant as possible without disturbing the cell pellet.
Keep the cell pellet on ice.
Mix by pipetting slowly to avoid bubbles.
Use the volumes in Table 2, adjusting according to the number of cells so that each hECT contains 1 million cells.
Prepare a 2.9 g/mL type-1 collagen solution in a 1.7 mL microtube.
Add 13.442 µL of distilled water to the microtube.
Add 4.4 µL of 10x PBS to the microtube.
Add 0.638 µL of 1M NaOH to the microtube.
Add 25.52 µL of 5 mg/mL collagen stock solution to the microtube.
Mix slowly until a uniform light-yellow to light-pink color is observed.
Prepare extracellular matrix mix (ECM mix from Table 2).
Add 5.5 µL of 0.2 N pH 9 HEPES solution to the ECM mix.
Add 5.5 µL of 10x MEM to the ECM mix.
Mix thoroughly until a uniform light-yellow to light-pink color is observed.
Transfer 35.2 µL of the ECM mix solution to the cell pellet.
Add 4.4 µL of basement membrane matrix to the cell pellet.
Open the autoclaved bag of bioreactor parts.
Remove the black baseplate from the autoclave bag and place it in a 60 mm dish with wells facing up.
Pipette 44 µL of cell mixture into each well slowly to avoid introducing bubbles.
Use pipette to remove any bubbles introduced by pipetting or due to hydrophobicity of PTFE.
Restore volume of hECT such that liquid surface is flush with lip of the well.
Remove polysulfone frame with PDMS racks from autoclave bag.
Lower the frame onto the baseplate ensuring ends fit into grooves at the ends of the baseplate.
Inspect bioreactor to ensure posts are straight and frame is not tilted before placing in 60 mm dish.
Add 1 mL of 10% FBS in cardiomyocyte maintenance medium to 60 mm dish without disturbing hECTs.
Place 60 mm dish into a high profile (20 mm tall) 100 mm dish, cover with 100 mm dish lid.
Return bioreactor to the 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator to allow collagen to form gel with cells in suspension.
After 2 h, remove the dish from the incubator.
Add 13 mL of 10% FBS in cardiomyocyte maintenance medium, tilting the dish to encourage flow between PTFE baseplate and PDMS racks.
Inspect bioreactor for air bubbles and return it to the incubator if no bubbles are trapped.
Tilt the bioreactor out of the medium or use a micropipette with gel loading tip to remove any trapped air bubbles carefully without disturbing posts.
Perform two half-volume medium changes when hECTs compact and become more opaque, changing medium to cardiomyocyte maintenance medium without FBS.
Remove baseplate when hECTs are compacted by at least 30% compared to original diameter.
Fill the 60 mm dish containing bioreactor with cardiomyocyte maintenance medium until liquid is flush with lip of dish, and add 14 mL to a new 60 mm dish.
Flip the bioreactor over in its dish so that baseplate is on top while wearing sterile gloves.
Inspect for trapped air bubbles as in step 3.2.8.
Slowly lift baseplate keeping it level.
If an hECT falls off during baseplate removal but remains in the baseplate, use sterile curved fine forceps to transfer the hECT from the baseplate into the 60 mm dish.
Use the forceps to guide the end of the hECT to its post.
Hold the post steady with a second pair of forceps and thread it through the hole in the hECT.
Repeat for the second post if necessary.
Transfer the frame with the hECTs to the new 60 mm dish, ensuring posts point down.
Inspect the bioreactor to ensure the hECTs remain on their posts just proximal to the SPoTs.
Stabilize the frame with a pair of sterile curved forceps if an hECT is pushed by surface tension to the base of its posts.
Insert another pair of forceps through the slot in the frame, keeping it closed.
Twist the tip of the inserted forceps so that it reaches the post once lowered past the PDMS racks.
Use the closed tips to gently push the hECT toward the end of the post until it rests on the SPoT.
Perform half-volume medium changes with cardiomyocyte maintenance medium every 24-48 hours after initial culture, reducing frequency to twice per week after two weeks.
Begin functional measurements when hECTs display clusters of spontaneous beating by day 3 and coordinated beating with visible post deflection by day 5.
Add distilled H2O to the mixture in specified volumes.
Add NaOH (1N) to the mixture in specified volumes.
Add PBS (10x) to the mixture in specified volumes.
Add collagen stock (5 mg/mL) to the mixture in specified volumes.
Add 0.2 N pH 9 HEPES to the mixture in specified volumes.
Add MEM (10x) to the mixture in specified volumes.
Transfer the ECM mix to the cell pellet as per volume specified.
Mix Matrigel with the cell mixture in specified volumes.
Use a laser cutting machine to cut acrylic insulating jacket components from a 0.635 cm thick clear acrylic sheet.
Assemble parts B, C, D, and one of E using acrylic glue as shown in Figure 5GI.
Attach the top panel (Figure 5GII).
Allow several hours for the glue to set.
Slide the heated stage into the side of the jacket (Figure 5GIII).
Secure the inserts between the legs of the heated stage with tape.
Add the front panel (Figure 5GIV) to finish the assembly (Figure 5GV).
Cut 6.25 mm thick, 25 mm wide graphite bars using a band saw into blocks 35 mm long.
Cut each block lengthwise in a curved line so that each electrode is 13-16 mm tall at one end and 8-10 mm tall at the other end.
Drill two 0.7 mm diameter holes in the upper corner (Figure 6AI).
Polish the pieces with paper towels.
Sonicate in water for 20 min to remove graphite dust.
Ensure that the electrodes wedge between the walls of the dish and the bioreactor to ensure a consistent distance between the electrodes (Figure 6AII).
Thread a 150 mm long x 0.25 mm diameter steel wire through the holes of the electrodes.
Bend the wire to fit over the lip of the 60 mm dish and around the walls of the 100 mm dish so that the lid can be closed (Figure 6AII).
Soak electrodes in distilled water for 1-2 h after each use.
Dry electrodes overnight after soaking.
Autoclave electrodes at 132 °C for 30 min before reuse.
Place one electrode on either side of the bioreactor.
Position wires so that the 100 mm dish lid can be closed.
Turn on the heated stage to 39.5 °C.
Set up pacing equipment on a vibration isolation table inside a laminar flow clean bench.
Mount the dissecting microscope on a boom stand.
Point the dissecting microscope at a right-angled mirror located on a lab jack below the glass table.
Affix a high-speed CCD camera to the microscope.
Connect the high-speed CCD camera to the computer.
Irradiate the setup with UV light for 15 min to sterilize the workspace.
Place the bioreactor on the jacketed heated stage.
Illuminate the bioreactor from above using a dual-head gooseneck LED light source.
Add a second 60 mm dish filled with prewarmed water inside of a 100 mm dish onto the heated table.
Outfit the second dish with a temperature probe for continuous monitoring.
Adjust the temperature setting of the heated stage to maintain the reference dish at 36-37 °C.
Set the microscope magnification to 1.5x or another desired magnification to visualize an hECT in its entirety with adequate resolution.
Open the camera software.
Resize the video feed to maximize the field of view while visualizing a whole hECT.
Set the capture rate to 90 frames per second.
Adjust the exposure time and light source position to optimize lighting uniformity and contrast of SPoTs.
Turn on the square pulse stimulator and connect it to the computer.
Adjust the settings to deliver biphasic pulses with an amplitude of 12 V and a duration of 5 ms.
Open the data acquisition software.
Open the "AutomatedPostTracking3.vi" file.
Click the white arrow in the toolbar to initialize the program.
Calibrate the software using a glass hemocytometer on the heated stage.
Draw a line across 1 mm of the hemocytometer markings.
Set the Reference length (mm) to 1 and click Calculate in the Distance calibration box.
Measure the hECT cross-sectional area by drawing a line across its width.
Click on the Cross-sectional area (mm^2) box to calculate the area.
Ensure the post tips are in focus.
Turn on the thresholding switch and adjust the slider until SPoTs are nicely demarcated and do not change shape as the hECT contracts.
Use the rectangle tool to draw a rectangle around one of the SPoTs.
Click on the Set 1 button inside the Post boundaries box to set the rectangle position around the SPoT.
Ensure that the SPoT remains within the boundary of the rectangle at all times.
Repeat for the other post and record it under Set 2.
Adjust the object size settings to prevent the program from tracking smaller objects.
Ensure that the number of objects tracked in each rectangle remains constant.
Monitor the noise using the interface showing the measured distance between tracked objects in real time.
Select a directory to save files.
Store data from different days in separate folders.
Select the current Tissue number and write any desired comments in the Comments box.
Indicate the range of frequencies desired under the Pacing Frequency header.
Specify the minimum and maximum pacing frequencies.
Define the interval for stepping from minimum to maximum frequency.
Test different pacing frequencies until a 1:1 stimulus:peak ratio is achieved.
Continue increasing the frequency until the 1:1 ratio is lost.
Measure spontaneous function by choosing an arbitrary frequency range of 0.01 Hz to 0.01 Hz.
Choose the desired setting time in seconds for hECT adjustment to new pacing frequency.
Specify recording time and pacing voltage.
Begin the program by clicking on the Start Program button.
Observe Fourier transformation display after each recording to confirm beating frequency detection.
Run the "Excitation Threshold Finding" program if necessary to find minimum required voltage.
Calculate maximum and minimum deflections of posts if necessary.
Mount the desired pair of PDMS racks onto a frame.
Use the pacing setup and software described in step 5.1 for functional measurements.
Select the stationary SPoTs at the ends of the posts.
Adjust the light source and/or thresholding if necessary to reduce noise to <2 µm.
Record the average live y-value indicated in the graph in a spreadsheet.
Remove the angled mirror and heated stage from the pacing setup described in step 5.2.
Place the bioreactor directly on the lab jack for a side view of the bioreactor.
Open the camera software.
Adjust the exposure time and light source position to optimize lighting uniformity across the field of view and maximize post visibility.
Open the data acquisition software.
Open the "PostMeasurement_PB3.vi" file (Supplementary File 5).
Click on the white arrow on the left side of the toolbar to initialize the program.
Calibrate the software using a glass hemocytometer.
Click on the line tool in the vertical toolbar and draw a line across 1 mm of the hemocytometer markings.
Set the Reference length (mm) to 1 in the Distance calibration (pixels/mm) box.
Click on the Calculate button.
Set the desired tissue number in the Tissue Number field.
Focus the camera on the left post of the hECT and select Left in the Post Side box.
Draw a line from the base of the post to the tip of the SPoTs, and record by clicking Measure Post Ht.
Draw a line from the base of the post to the far edge of the hECT, and record by clicking Measure Tissue Top Ht.
Draw a line from the base of the post to the near edge of the hECT, and record by clicking Measure Tissue Base Ht.
Turn the bioreactor around to measure the right post height.
Select the right post option to record the same measurements.
Click on the Add button to populate the spreadsheet with the measured values and automatically calculate the average height of the hECT.
Once finished recording the tissue heights, click on the Save button to save the values to a text file.
Fill out the summary file using the template in a spreadsheet editor.
Ensure that all the hECTs that have data in the folder are represented in the summary file.
Name the file "summary #.csv", where # refers to the number of days into the experiment.
Ensure the folder containing the AnalyzeLogsGUI scripts is added to the path.
Add the folder with the hECT recordings to the path.
Open the data analysis software.
Click on the Browse for folder button to navigate to the parent folder that contains both the AnalyzeLogsGUI folder and the hECT functional data.
Right-click on these folders in the Current Window sidebar and add them to the path.
Open the "AnalyzeLogsGui_SC.m" file.
Press the Run button in the Editor tab.
Wait for the graphical user interface (GUI) to appear in a new window.
Click the Select Directory button in the Log Selection box.
Navigate to the folder that includes the hECT functional data and select it.
Select the desired hECT to be processed from the Tissue dropdown menu.
Input the unloaded distance between the posts recorded from steps 6.1 into the Diastolic Distance field.
Input 0.25 in the Post Radius (mm) field.
Choose the frequencies to omit or include for analysis in the Analysis Constraints box.
Set the start time and end time to 0 and −1, respectively, to process the whole length of the recordings if necessary.
Change the start time and end time values to trim the recordings if needed.
Change filter parameters for Polynomial Order and Frame Size to adjust smoothing level during filtering.
Adjust Peak Detection Threshold slider to set minimum peak size recognized by scripts.
Use trimming of recordings instead of Spike Removal option to avoid changing twitch shapes.
Enable Post deflection analysis to run an additional peak detection algorithm.
Select Autoscale y-axis on zoom plots to automatically adjust axes on twitch force curve.
Choose Save force-trace curves to save each twitch force figure as a .fig file.
Select Save force-time data to save x- and y-coordinates of filtered data plotted in twitch force curve figure.
Click Run Analysis to generate a .txt file containing averaged attributes of the twitch force curve.
